quick.topic: Set a date to delete data
quick.summary: Why keeping everything forever is a risk, and how a retention rule works.
quick.takeaway: Decide how long each kind of data is kept, then delete on schedule.

parts.title: Set a date to delete data

beats.line: We still store customer addresses from accounts closed five years ago. Is that a problem?

board.text: Set a date to delete data

beats.line: Yes. Data you keep can leak, and many privacy laws limit how long.
The fix is a retention rule. Three parts.
Can I call it a keep until date?
Good. A keep until date, for each kind of data.
What kind of data. How long it is kept. And a job to delete it.

board.text: what · how long · a delete job

beats.line: The period comes from legal, not from you.
Closed account addresses: kept the agreed period, then deleted by a monthly job.
Less to store, less to leak, and easier to defend.

quiz.question: Who should decide how long personal data is kept?
options: Legal or compliance, with the rule then built into a job
quiz.explanation: How long data may be kept is a legal question; engineering implements the agreed rule.

quiz.question: Keeping all personal data forever is the safest choice.
quiz.explanation: Stored data can leak, and privacy rules often limit how long it may be kept.
